text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Interior Minister Mansour says June 5 parliamentary poll will usher in era of multiparty democracy and state of law.
- Government considers increasing water price in attempt to streamline state-owned water utility.

- Political leaders to kick off campaign on Thursday; Abdallah Djaballa of Nahda movement will hold rally in southern town of Djelfa; Said Saadi, head of Rally for Culture and Democracy, meets supporters in Algiers; Movement for a Peaceful Society's leader Mahfoud Nahnah presides over rally in Boumerdes near Algiers; former minister Redha Malek holds meeting with his National Republican Alliance party members in Medea.
- Political parties worry about control of security forces' vote. Soldiers and police will vote in barracks and stations, making it difficult for political groups to oversee polling.
